question_text: Which diseases of the vine are the greatest threat to vineyards around the world today, and why?
command_word_demand: Examiners were looking for a good understanding of disease threats around the world showing global knowledge and analysis as to why and how they are a threat.

required_elements.element: Show global knowledge of disease threats, with analysis of why and how they are a threat
required_elements.quote: Examiners were looking for a good understanding of disease threats around the world showing global knowledge and analysis as to why and how they are a threat.

required_elements.element: Analyse why diseases are a threat, not just describe them
required_elements.quote: The main negative comments for this question were that many students, while showing good knowledge of the different diseases of the vine, failed to analyse why they were a threat.

required_elements.element: Provide detail on the nature of the threat: economic cost, spread, and impact on long-term vineyard success
required_elements.quote: Candidates were required not only to show a knowledge of the diseases, but to provide detail on the nature of their threat: economic cost, spread, and impact on the long-term success of vineyards.

credit_signals.signal: Combining textbook knowledge of how diseases work and are managed with discussion of how and why they are a threat, showing critical thinking
credit_signals.quote: Most impressive was when candidates combined the textbook knowledge of how the diseases work and what is being done to manage them with a discussion of how and why they are a threat to vineyards, thus showing the critical thinking needed to pass the MW exam.

penalty_signals.signal: Examples devoted only to how producers manage diseases, without analysis of the threat itself
penalty_signals.quote: A lot of examples were devoted only to how producers are managing diseases without analysis of the threat.

penalty_signals.signal: Omitting less well-known but significant diseases
penalty_signals.quote: Better-known diseases like mildews and trunk disease were generally well covered but often other diseases like Red Blotch, Pierce's Disease and Flavescence Dorée were omitted.

penalty_signals.signal: Just describing various diseases without analysis
penalty_signals.quote: The less successful candidates just described various diseases.

examples_expected.specificity: Named specific vine diseases, including less common ones beyond the well-known mildews/trunk disease
examples_expected.quote: Better-known diseases like mildews and trunk disease were generally well covered but often other diseases like Red Blotch, Pierce's Disease and Flavescence Dorée were omitted.

performance_note: Question 1 had the highest average mark of all Paper 1 questions and answers were of a generally high standard.

question_text: What effects do vineyard pests have on grape quality, and how do grape growers control them?
command_word_demand: For this question examiners were looking for a broad understanding of the different vineyard pests and how they are controlled, linking the impact back to grape quality.

required_elements.element: Explicitly link pest impacts to grape quality, not wine quality
required_elements.quote: While most candidates showed knowledge of a number of vineyard pests and control options, too often the link to grape quality was weak or non-existent. Some candidates discussed wine quality rather than grape quality and others missed making the link altogether.

required_elements.element: Show global understanding that different pests have different impacts in different regions, with different control options
required_elements.quote: There are many different vineyard pests and they have different impacts in different regions of the world. To be successful a student needed to show this global understanding and show the different control options in a range of situations.

required_elements.element: Cover the key vineyard pests, not just a partial selection
required_elements.quote: Nearly every candidate missed considering some of the key pests, so despite some generally good essays, there were often holes that were too big to warrant a passing grade.

penalty_signals.signal: Misunderstandings of basic plant, insect and pathogen biology, vine physiology, disease impacts and vectors
penalty_signals.quote: There were many misunderstandings relating to the basic biology of plants, insects and pathogens, vine physiology, insects, disease impacts and vectors.

penalty_signals.signal: Essays reading as a list of pests with one treatment each, without deeper analysis
penalty_signals.quote: Many essays just read as a list of pests with one possible treatment for each.

penalty_signals.signal: Vague, broad examples that did not show deep understanding
penalty_signals.quote: Examples were often too vague and too broad, not being specific enough to show a deep understanding.

examples_expected.specificity: Specific rather than vague or broad, sufficient to show a deep understanding
examples_expected.quote: Examples were often too vague and too broad, not being specific enough to show a deep understanding.

scope_traps.trap: Discussing wine quality instead of grape quality (or failing to make the link at all)
scope_traps.quote: Some candidates discussed wine quality rather than grape quality and others missed making the link altogether.

question_text: To what extent does the geology of a vineyard affect the way it is managed?
command_word_demand: This question required candidates to take a broad look at all aspects of vineyard management to identify to what extent the geology of a vineyard impacts, for example, drainage, irrigation, CEC, nutrition, weed control, vigour, fertilizers, vineyard equipment, vine trellising, erosion, tilling and cover crops.

definitions_required.quote: Some candidates seemed to be confused about how a soil's texture differs from its geological makeup and how these things have different impacts on management.

required_elements.element: Take a broad look at all aspects of vineyard management affected by geology (e.g. drainage, irrigation, CEC, nutrition, weed control, vigour, fertilizers, vineyard equipment, vine trellising, erosion, tilling, cover crops)
required_elements.quote: This question required candidates to take a broad look at all aspects of vineyard management to identify to what extent the geology of a vineyard impacts, for example, drainage, irrigation, CEC, nutrition, weed control, vigour, fertilizers, vineyard equipment, vine trellising, erosion, tilling and cover crops.

required_elements.element: Link geology, soil, and management together rather than treating them separately
required_elements.quote: There was a tendency to write either about geology, soil, or management, with few candidates linking it all together as required by the question.

required_elements.element: Properly weigh "to what extent" and touch on a broad variety of management situations
required_elements.quote: The passing papers considered "to what extent" well, and touched on a broad variety of management situations.

penalty_signals.signal: Writing about geology, soil, or management in isolation instead of linking them together
penalty_signals.quote: There was a tendency to write either about geology, soil, or management, with few candidates linking it all together as required by the question.

penalty_signals.signal: Confusing soil texture with geological makeup and their differing management impacts
penalty_signals.quote: Some candidates seemed to be confused about how a soil's texture differs from its geological makeup and how these things have different impacts on management.

examples_expected.specificity: A broad variety of management situations linked to geology, e.g. drainage, irrigation, CEC, nutrition, weed control, vigour, fertilizers, vineyard equipment, vine trellising, erosion, tilling and cover crops
examples_expected.quote: This question required candidates to take a broad look at all aspects of vineyard management to identify to what extent the geology of a vineyard impacts, for example, drainage, irrigation, CEC, nutrition, weed control, vigour, fertilizers, vineyard equipment, vine trellising, erosion, tilling and cover crops.

question_text: Glyphosate use is coming under increasing scrutiny. Should it be banned in modern viticulture? What are the alternatives?
command_word_demand: This question was designed to test a candidate's ability to be able to consider all sides of the issue in a non-biased way, yet clearly come down with an opinion on whether it should be banned. This skill is paramount in passing any MW paper.

required_elements.element: Consider all sides of the glyphosate issue in a non-biased way, yet clearly come down with an opinion on whether it should be banned
required_elements.quote: This question was designed to test a candidate's ability to be able to consider all sides of the issue in a non-biased way, yet clearly come down with an opinion on whether it should be banned. This skill is paramount in passing any MW paper.

required_elements.element: Discuss alternatives with a broad understanding, including financial and logistical implications and long-term vineyard health
required_elements.quote: The best answers did just that, discussing the pros and cons objectively, showing a broad understanding of alternatives and considering financial and logistical implications, as well as the long-term health of the vineyard.

credit_signals.signal: Discussing pros and cons objectively, with a broad understanding of alternatives and consideration of financial, logistical and long-term vineyard-health implications
credit_signals.quote: The best answers did just that, discussing the pros and cons objectively, showing a broad understanding of alternatives and considering financial and logistical implications, as well as the long-term health of the vineyard.

penalty_signals.signal: Letting personal opinion show without properly unbiased consideration of pros and cons, referencing only headline statements
penalty_signals.quote: Some candidates clearly let their personal opinions be known without showing proper unbiased consideration of the pros and cons, often referencing only headline statements without going any deeper.

penalty_signals.signal: Answers full of examples and information but completely one-sided
penalty_signals.quote: Many answers were full of examples and information but completely one-sided.

question_text: As a viticulturist, what factors would influence your approach to growing cover crops in a vineyard?
command_word_demand: Successful candidates showed an understanding of the purpose of using a cover crop, the limiting factors (such as climate, irrigation, soil type, planting density, microclimate, humidity/temperature, and vine details such as age, vigour, health, etc.), the cover crop options and timing of when to use them.

required_elements.element: Show understanding of the purpose of using a cover crop, limiting factors, the cover crop options available, and timing of use
required_elements.quote: Successful candidates showed an understanding of the purpose of using a cover crop, the limiting factors (such as climate, irrigation, soil type, planting density, microclimate, humidity/temperature, and vine details such as age, vigour, health, etc.), the cover crop options and timing of when to use them.

required_elements.element: Analyse and explain why different cover crop options work in one situation but not another, supported by a broad range of global examples
required_elements.quote: Importantly, different cover crop options may work in one situation but not in another and this needed to be analysed and explained, supported by a broad range of global examples.

required_elements.element: Consider the full list of relevant factors: soil water, soil temperature, drainage, frost, nutrients, pests/IPM, humidity, vigour, erosion, compaction, equipment access, cultivation and financial aspects
required_elements.quote: To be successful, candidates needed to consider things like soil water, soil temperature, drainage, frost, nutrients, pests/IPM, humidity, vigour, erosion, compaction, equipment access, cultivation and financial aspects.

required_elements.element: Show understanding that cover crops carry simultaneous risks and rewards
required_elements.quote: Cover crops can also have simultaneous risks and rewards, and the best papers showed an understanding of this.

credit_signals.signal: Understanding that cover crops carry simultaneous risks and rewards
credit_signals.quote: Cover crops can also have simultaneous risks and rewards, and the best papers showed an understanding of this.

penalty_signals.signal: Essays filled with examples of what producers do regarding cover crops without critical analysis of why
penalty_signals.quote: In many cases, essays were filled with lots of examples of what viticulturists/producers do regarding the use of cover crops without much critical analysis of why.

penalty_signals.signal: Only top-level understanding of this complex, multi-area question
penalty_signals.quote: For many candidates, this quite complex question, touching on many areas of grape growing, highlighted only a top-level understanding of viticulture.

penalty_signals.signal: Showing only one side of the risk/reward equation, or too top-level and lacking detail
penalty_signals.quote: The less successful papers showed only one side of the equation or were too top-level, lacking sufficient detail.

examples_expected.specificity: A broad range of global examples showing why different cover crop options work in different situations
examples_expected.quote: Importantly, different cover crop options may work in one situation but not in another and this needed to be analysed and explained, supported by a broad range of global examples.

performance_note: This was the most popular question amongst candidates, but answers were mixed.

question_text: What factors affect the timing of pruning in vineyards around the world?
command_word_demand: this tested an understanding of different pruning considerations globally based on unique situations in vineyards across the world.

required_elements.element: Show global understanding that pruning-timing factors vary by region (e.g. winter damage in extreme regions, rainfall, frost risk, labour logistics)
required_elements.quote: This could be potential winter damage in extreme regions, rainfall in others, frost risk somewhere else or labour logistics, for example.

required_elements.element: Address both dormant and green pruning and the influence of timing on bud break
required_elements.quote: Timing of pruning and its potential influence on bud break is crucial. Trunk disease risk and attempting to hedge against unpredictable climate needed consideration, along with both dormant and green pruning.

required_elements.element: Link green pruning timing to growth, ripeness, pests/diseases and wine style
required_elements.quote: Most candidates demonstrated a good understanding of dormant pruning and its timing but fewer made the link with green pruning and how its timing might influence growth, ripeness, pests and diseases and wine style.

penalty_signals.signal: Failing to mention green pruning at all
penalty_signals.quote: A few candidates failed to mention green pruning at all, reducing the potential for higher marks in otherwise strong papers.

penalty_signals.signal: Drifting into pruning method or frost management, which was not helpful to answering the question
penalty_signals.quote: A lot of essays drifted off into method of pruning (which was relevant only if linking things like mechanical pruning to speed), or into topics such as frost management which was not helpful to answer the question.

penalty_signals.signal: Assuming bud break happens at the same time everywhere in the world and that fires/hail occur on a predictable schedule
penalty_signals.quote: Some candidates seemed to think bud break happens at the same time everywhere in the world and that fires and hail happen on a regular schedule that you can prune around.

penalty_signals.signal: Parroting information heard from producers without understanding why or when such actions are appropriate
penalty_signals.quote: Many papers seemed only to have top-level knowledge of pruning considerations and some candidates seemed to be just parroting back information they had heard from producers without understanding why, or when such actions may or may not be appropriate.

scope_traps.trap: Drifting into pruning method (e.g. mechanical vs. hand) or frost management instead of addressing timing
scope_traps.quote: A lot of essays drifted off into method of pruning (which was relevant only if linking things like mechanical pruning to speed), or into topics such as frost management which was not helpful to answer the question.

performance_note: The second most popular question, this tested an understanding of different pruning considerations globally based on unique situations in vineyards across the world.
